newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: FOCUS-Venezuelan electricity system is collapsing.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Venezuelan electricity system is collapsing.

text.p: Venezuelan ministers and state- owned company officials are adding their voices to private sector calls for swift tariff hikes and a clear set of rules for the country's collapsing electricity distribution system.

Lack of a regulatory framework -- combined with years of inefficiency, corruption and steep financial losses -- make planned electricity privatizations slated for later this year extremely unlikely, officials said.

And while Venezuela's privatization agency, the Venezuelan Investment Fund (FIV) has already earmarked 13.4 billion bolivars ($27 million) in investments for three companies in its portfolio -- Enelbar, Enelven and Enelco -- such investments only paper over the problem and do not go to the heart of the issue, FIV president Alberto Poletto said.
"There's no chance of privatization unless the sector's regulatory framework is clear and firm," Poletto told reporters late Wednesday after a congressional presentation on the sector.
"The system is collapsing," Energy and Mines Congressional Commission chief Ali Rodriguez said.
"It's been decapitalized as the government thought it could easily privatize the companies," he said.
But that prospect is now unlikely, even though the Energy and Mines and Ministry presented a regulatory draft to Congress last week for discussion.

Hydro-electric generating colosus Edelca, which provides 70 percent of the country's energy as well as power to huge state- owned steel and aluminum firms in southwestern Venezuela, has also asked for the government to approve a 50 percent tariff hike.
"That's what we need to make up for past inflation," Edelca president Efrain Carrera said. Inflation in 1996 topped 100 percent and this year is officially targeted at 35 percent.
Normally, calls for tariff hikes are limited to private sector companies, such as stock market bellwether Electricidad de Caracas.
According to government officials, guidelines for adjusting tariffs have been prepared and are now waiting on government approval.
